title: Your own story
job: An eight-sentence account, built from the whole ladder
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 4.5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: imperfetto — the standing situation, L2-M10's tense
passato prossimo — each completed step, L1-M5's tense
present — only for the sentence that lands in now

rules.text: THE IMPERFETTO PAINTS, THE PASSATO PROSSIMO MOVES. Everything that was already true when the account starts goes in the imperfetto — ero in stazione, pioveva, c'era molta gente — and every completed step that pushes the story forward goes in the passato prossimo: è arrivato, ho preso, sono tornato. L2-M10 opened this pair over four sentences; eight is where a learner finds out whether they have it. Nothing new is opened for it here.

MENTRE ALWAYS TAKES THE IMPERFETTO, AND WHAT INTERRUPTS IT TAKES THE PASSATO PROSSIMO. Mentre aspettavo, è arrivato un collega — the waiting was going on, the arriving cut into it. Two passato prossimos in a row would say the two things simply happened one after the other, which is a different account. This is the sharpest minimal pair in the level, and the sentence a learner most often gets half right.

ESSERE OR AVERE, AND ONLY ESSERE AGREES. Movement, change of state and reflexives take essere, and the participle then agrees with the SUBJECT: sono arrivato from a man, sono arrivata from a woman, siamo arrivati from a group. Everything else takes avere and the participle never moves: ho preso, ho fatto, ho capito, whoever is speaking. An eight-sentence account uses both a dozen times, which is why this is the module where guessing stops working.

THE CONNECTORS ARE THE WHOLE HONEST SPEND OF THIS MODULE: all'inizio (at first), poi (then, L1-M10's), mentre (while), appena (as soon as) and alla fine (in the end, L2-M10's). Five words turn a list of sentences into an account, and everything else here has already been paid for further down the ladder.

ENGLISH HAS ONE PAST WHERE ITALIAN HAS TWO, so a learner picks by feel and picks the same one every time. The test is not how it sounds: swap one verb from imperfetto to passato prossimo and ask whether WHAT HAPPENED changed. Aspettavo il treno says the waiting was still going on; ho aspettato il treno says it finished. Both are correct Italian and they are different stories.

sentences.display: Ieri ero in stazione. Aspettavo il treno per Milano. Mentre aspettavo, è arrivato un collega. Ho parlato con lui un po'. Poi è partito il treno. Alla fine sono tornato a casa tardi.
sentences.cue: Yesterday I was at the station. I was waiting for the train to Milan. While I was waiting, a colleague arrived. I talked with him for a bit. Then the train left. In the end I got home late.
sentences.literal: Yesterday I-was in station. I-was-waiting the train for Milan. While I-was-waiting, is arrived a colleague. I-have talked with him a bit. Then is left the train. At-the end I-am returned at home late.

words.note: Always followed by an imperfetto. What cuts into it goes in the passato prossimo — that split is the whole point of the word.
The imperfetto of L3-M5's aspettare. It says the waiting was still going on, which is why mentre can hang something off it.
Movement, so it takes essere and agrees with the subject: è arrivata una collega, sono arrivati due colleghi.

sentences.trap: Ho aspettato il treno e è arrivato un collega tells a different story: the waiting finished, and then somebody turned up. mentre is what makes one thing cut into the other.
sentences.sound: MEN-tre as-pet-TA-vo, e ar-ri-VA-to oon kol-LE-ga. mentre is two syllables, stressed on the first.

variations.display: Mentre aspettavo, è arrivata una collega
variations.cue: While I was waiting, a colleague arrived
variations.changed: a woman arriving, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Ho preso il treno e ho parlato con lui
variations.cue: I took the train and talked with him
variations.changed: two finished steps, so no mentre and no imperfetto

variations.display: Mentre tornavo a casa, è arrivato un messaggio
variations.cue: While I was going home, a message arrived
variations.changed: a different pair of actions

mistake.display: Mentre ho aspettato, è arrivato un collega
mistake.why: mentre takes the imperfetto: Mentre aspettavo, è arrivato un collega.

sentences.usage: The everyday shape of a small story about a delay — scene, interruption, ending.

sentences.display: Stamattina pioveva. Non avevo la macchina. Ho preso l'autobus. C'era molta gente. Ho fatto tardi in ufficio. Purtroppo la riunione era finita.
sentences.cue: This morning it was raining. I did not have the car. I took the bus. There were a lot of people. I was late to the office. Unfortunately the meeting had finished.
sentences.literal: This-morning it-was-raining. Not I-had the car. I-have taken the-bus. There-was much people. I-have made late in office. Unfortunately the meeting was finished.

words.note: The participle of fare, and irregular. It takes avere and never agrees: ho fatto, ha fatto, abbiamo fatto. fare tardi is "to be late".
With essere it means a thing came to an end and agrees with it: la riunione era finita. With avere it means somebody finished something: ho finito il lavoro.

sentences.trap: Four of these six verbs are imperfetto and two are passato prossimo, and English writes all six the same way. The rain, the missing car and the crowd were the situation; taking the bus and being late were the steps.
sentences.sound: sta-mat-TEE-na pyo-VE-va. o FAT-to TAR-dee een uf-FEE-cho. pioveva runs as one long word.

variations.display: Stamattina pioveva e ho preso l'autobus
variations.cue: This morning it was raining and I took the bus
variations.changed: scene and step in one sentence

variations.display: Ho fatto tardi perché c'era molta gente
variations.cue: I was late because there were a lot of people
variations.changed: the reason attached with L1-M9's perché

variations.display: Ho finito il lavoro tardi
variations.cue: I finished the work late
variations.changed: finire with avere, so no agreement

mistake.display: Stamattina ha piovuto e non ho avuto la macchina
mistake.why: The rain and the missing car were the situation, not steps: Stamattina pioveva. Non avevo la macchina.

sentences.usage: The standard apology for arriving late, in the order an Italian tells it.
sentences.mnemonic: Situation in the imperfetto, steps in the passato prossimo.

sentences.display: All'inizio non avevo amici a Milano. Lavoravo molto e tornavo tardi. Poi ho trovato una collega simpatica. Adesso ho molti amici e Milano mi piace molto.
sentences.cue: At first I had no friends in Milan. I worked a lot and came home late. Then I found a nice colleague. Now I have a lot of friends and I like Milan a lot.
sentences.literal: At-the-beginning not I-had friends at Milan. I-worked much and I-returned late. Then I-have found a colleague nice. Now I-have many friends and Milan to-me it-pleases much.

words.note: One word once the elision is written in, and it opens an account the way alla fine closes one. It always leads into the imperfetto.
The participle of trovare, regular and taking avere, so it never agrees: ho trovato, ha trovato.

sentences.trap: The first two sentences are how things stood for months, so both are imperfetto. A learner who puts ho lavorato there has said the working stopped, which turns a settling-in story into a resignation.
sentences.sound: al-lee-NEE-tsyo. The apostrophe is not a pause: all'inizio is four syllables run together.

variations.display: All'inizio lavoravo molto, adesso sto meglio
variations.cue: At first I worked a lot, now I am better
variations.changed: then against now, in one sentence

variations.display: Poi ho trovato un lavoro nuovo
variations.cue: Then I found a new job
variations.changed: a different step

variations.display: All'inizio ero preoccupato, alla fine sono stato bene
variations.cue: At first I was worried, in the end I was fine
variations.changed: both connectors together

mistake.display: All'inizio non ho avuto amici a Milano
mistake.why: That was the standing situation, not one event: All'inizio non avevo amici a Milano.

sentences.usage: How anybody tells the story of moving somewhere — the hard start, the turn, the now.

sentences.display: Appena sono arrivato a Roma, ho chiamato mia madre. Era molto contenta. Poi ho preso un caffè al bar. Faceva caldo. Sono andato a casa di mia sorella.
sentences.cue: As soon as I arrived in Rome, I called my mother. She was very happy. Then I had a coffee at the bar. It was hot. I went to my sister's house.
sentences.literal: As-soon-as I-am arrived at Rome, I-have called my mother. She-was very happy. Then I-have taken a coffee at-the bar. It-made hot. I-am gone at house of my sister.

words.note: Unlike mentre it takes the passato prossimo, because both things are finished steps: appena sono arrivato, ho chiamato.

sentences.trap: appena and mentre look like the same kind of word and take opposite tenses. mentre needs something still going on; appena needs two things that both finished, one right after the other.
sentences.sound: ap-PE-na SO-no ar-ri-VA-to a RO-ma. appena holds its double p.

variations.display: Appena sono arrivata, ho chiamato mia madre
variations.cue: As soon as I arrived, I called my mother
variations.changed: a woman speaking, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Appena ho finito, sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: As soon as I finished, I went home
variations.changed: a different pair of steps

variations.display: Mentre aspettavo, ho preso un caffè
variations.cue: While I was waiting, I had a coffee
variations.changed: mentre instead, so the first verb goes imperfetto

mistake.display: Appena arrivavo a Roma, ho chiamato mia madre
mistake.why: appena takes the passato prossimo: Appena sono arrivato a Roma, ho chiamato mia madre.

sentences.usage: The opening of any account of a journey, and the natural way to report a chain of arrivals.

sentences.display: Ho cominciato a lavorare in una ditta nuova. Il primo giorno ero molto preoccupato. Non c'era nessuno in ufficio. Poi è arrivato il capo. Mi ha detto di aspettare. Alla fine ho lavorato tutto il giorno.
sentences.cue: I started working at a new company. The first day I was very worried. There was nobody in the office. Then the boss arrived. He told me to wait. In the end I worked all day.
sentences.literal: I-have begun at to-work in a company new. The first day I-was very worried. Not there-was nobody in office. Then is arrived the boss. To-me he-has said of to-wait. At-the end I-have worked all the day.

words.note: Takes avere when somebody starts something — ho cominciato a lavorare — and the a before the infinitive is fixed.

sentences.trap: cominciare takes a before an infinitive where L3-M5's dire and L1-M9's pensare take di. There is no rule to derive it from; the preposition belongs to the verb.
sentences.sound: o ko-min-CHA-to a la-vo-RA-re. The ci in cominciato is a soft ch.

variations.display: Ho cominciato a lavorare lunedì
variations.cue: I started working on Monday
variations.changed: when, with a bare day

variations.display: La riunione è cominciata tardi
variations.cue: The meeting started late
variations.changed: essere, because the meeting started by itself, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Mentre aspettavo, è arrivato il capo
variations.cue: While I was waiting, the boss arrived
variations.changed: the same arrival, told as an interruption

mistake.display: Ho cominciato lavorare in una ditta nuova
mistake.why: cominciare needs its a: Ho cominciato a lavorare in una ditta nuova.

sentences.usage: The first-day story, which everybody is asked for and everybody tells the same way.

sentences.display: Stasera è successo un problema con il treno. Aspettavo in stazione. Il treno non è arrivato. C'era molta gente e faceva freddo. Alla fine ho preso l'autobus. Sono tornato a casa alle sette.
sentences.cue: This evening there was a problem with the train. I was waiting at the station. The train did not arrive. There were a lot of people and it was cold. In the end I took the bus. I got home at seven.
sentences.literal: This-evening is happened a problem with the train. I-was-waiting in station. The train not is arrived. There-was much people and it-made cold. At-the end I-have taken the-bus. I-am returned at home at-the seven.

words.note: The participle of succedere, always with essere: è successo un problema. Che cosa è successo? is how you ask what happened.

sentences.trap: English "there was a problem" looks like a description and would tempt an imperfetto. è successo is a step: the problem arrived at a moment, and the account starts there.
sentences.sound: e suc-CES-so oon pro-BLE-ma. successo holds its double c and its double s.

variations.display: Che cosa è successo?
variations.cue: What happened?
variations.changed: asked as a question

variations.display: Ieri è successo un problema in ufficio
variations.cue: Yesterday there was a problem at the office
variations.changed: when and where

variations.display: Stasera è successa una cosa
variations.cue: Something happened this evening
variations.changed: a feminine subject, so the participle agrees

mistake.display: Stasera ha successo un problema con il treno
mistake.why: succedere always takes essere: Stasera è successo un problema con il treno.

sentences.usage: The way any story about a delay or a mishap opens, before the detail.

sentences.display: Lunedì stavo male. Avevo la febbre e mal di gola. Non sono andato in ufficio. Sono rimasto a casa. Ho dormito tutto il giorno. Adesso sto bene.
sentences.cue: On Monday I was unwell. I had a fever and a sore throat. I did not go to the office. I stayed at home. I slept all day. Now I am fine.
sentences.literal: Monday I-was bad. I-had the fever and bad of throat. Not I-am gone in office. I-am stayed at home. I-have slept all the day. Now I-am well.

words.note: The imperfetto of L1-M2's sto. Health takes stare, not essere: sto bene, stavo male — ero male is not said.

sentences.trap: Being unwell is stare, not essere. ero male is the sentence an English speaker builds and an Italian does not recognise; the verb for how you are is the one in come stai?
sentences.sound: lu-ne-DEE STA-vo MA-le. stavo is stressed on the STA.

variations.display: Stavo male, poi sono stato meglio
variations.cue: I was unwell, then I got better
variations.changed: the turn, with the participle of stare

variations.display: Mio figlio stava male e sono rimasto a casa
variations.cue: My son was unwell and I stayed at home
variations.changed: somebody else unwell, and the consequence

variations.display: Sono rimasta a casa tutto il giorno
variations.cue: I stayed at home all day
variations.changed: a woman speaking, so the participle agrees

mistake.why: Health takes stare: Lunedì stavo male.

sentences.usage: What you tell a colleague on the day you come back.

sentences.display: Ieri è venuto un amico a casa mia. Ha parlato molto in italiano. All'inizio non ho capito bene. Poi ho capito tutto. Alla fine sono molto contento.
sentences.cue: Yesterday a friend came to my house. He talked a lot in Italian. At first I did not understand well. Then I understood everything. In the end I am very happy.
sentences.literal: Yesterday is come a friend at house my. He-has talked much in Italian. At-the-beginning not I-have understood well. Then I-have understood all. At-the end I-am very happy.

words.note: Movement, so essere and agreement with the subject: è venuta una collega. The participle is irregular; the infinitive is venire.
The participle of capire, taking avere and never agreeing. Ho capito on its own is the commonest "got it" in the language.

sentences.trap: venuto takes essere and capito takes avere, and both sit in the same account. The auxiliary belongs to the verb, not to the sentence, so it has to be learnt one verb at a time.
sentences.sound: e ve-NOO-to oon a-MEE-ko. o ka-PEE-to TOOT-to. Both participles are stressed on the syllable before the ending.

variations.display: Ieri è venuta una collega a casa mia
variations.cue: Yesterday a colleague came to my house
variations.changed: a woman coming, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Non ho capito, può ripetere?
variations.cue: I did not understand, can you repeat that?
variations.changed: asked politely, with L2-M1's ripetere

variations.display: Appena è venuto, ho capito tutto
variations.cue: As soon as he came, I understood everything
variations.changed: the two steps chained with appena

mistake.display: Ieri ha venuto un amico a casa mia
mistake.why: venire takes essere: Ieri è venuto un amico a casa mia.

sentences.usage: A small, warm account of an evening — and the sentence Ho capito is worth having on its own.
sentences.mnemonic: venire comes with essere; capire takes avere.

sentences.display: Ieri ho scritto un messaggio a mia sorella. Non ha letto il messaggio. Ho lavorato tutto il giorno. Stasera ha chiamato. Era in ufficio. Adesso è tutto a posto.
sentences.cue: Yesterday I wrote a message to my sister. She did not read the message. I worked all day. This evening she called. She was at the office. Now everything is fine.
sentences.literal: Yesterday I-have written a message at my sister. Not she-has read the message. I-have worked all the day. This-evening she-has called. She-was in office. Now is all at place.

words.note: The irregular participle of scrivere, with avere and no agreement. The double t is what makes it audible.
The irregular participle of leggere, with avere. Spelt exactly like the noun for a bed, which context always sorts out.

sentences.trap: Era in ufficio is the one imperfetto in the account and it is doing real work: it explains why she did not read, rather than adding a step. Turn it into è stata in ufficio and the explanation disappears.
sentences.sound: o SKREET-to oon mes-SAJ-jo. non a LET-to. Both participles hold a double consonant.

variations.display: Ho scritto un messaggio al capo
variations.cue: I wrote a message to the boss
variations.changed: who it was written to

variations.display: Non ho letto il messaggio, purtroppo
variations.cue: I did not read the message, unfortunately
variations.changed: the reader, and an apology attached

variations.display: Mentre lavoravo, ha chiamato mia sorella
variations.cue: While I was working, my sister called
variations.changed: told as an interruption with mentre

mistake.display: Ieri ho scritto un messaggio e era in ufficio
mistake.why: The explanation needs its own sentence, and era stays imperfetto: Non ha letto il messaggio. Era in ufficio.

sentences.usage: The everyday account of a message that went unanswered, and its harmless explanation.
sentences.mnemonic: The imperfetto explains; the passato prossimo happens.

sentences.display: Ho dovuto pagare l'affitto entro venerdì. Non avevo i soldi. Ho chiesto aiuto a mio padre. Mi ha detto di aspettare. Alla fine ho fatto un bonifico. Adesso sono tranquillo.
sentences.cue: I had to pay the rent by Friday. I did not have the money. I asked my father for help. He told me to wait. In the end I made a bank transfer. Now I am calm.
sentences.literal: I-have had-to to-pay the-rent within Friday. Not I-had the money. I-have asked help at my father. To-me he-has said of to-wait. At-the end I-have made a transfer. Now I-am calm.

words.note: The participle of devo. In the past a modal keeps its infinitive after it: ho dovuto pagare, ho potuto pagare, ho voluto pagare.

sentences.trap: Non avevo i soldi is the situation and every other verb here is a step. This is the level's exit test in one sentence: if that verb comes out as non ho avuto, the account has stopped explaining and started listing.
sentences.sound: o do-VOO-to pa-GA-re laf-FEET-to. dovuto is stressed on the VOO.

variations.display: Ho dovuto pagare la bolletta entro martedì
variations.cue: I had to pay the bill by Tuesday
variations.changed: a different bill and a different day

variations.display: Non ho potuto pagare, non avevo i soldi
variations.cue: I could not pay, I did not have the money
variations.changed: potere instead of dovere

variations.display: Mio padre mi ha detto di aspettare
variations.cue: My father told me to wait
variations.changed: the person doing the telling named

mistake.display: Ho dovuto pagato l'affitto entro venerdì
mistake.why: A modal keeps the infinitive after it: Ho dovuto pagare l'affitto entro venerdì.

sentences.usage: The account of a month that was tight and came out fine — and the last sentence of the level.
sentences.mnemonic: ho dovuto + infinitive, never a second participle.
